extracts.lead_summary: A correction first. Last Friday I called $99.04 the November contract; it was already December. November settled $101.41 — a $9.56 week, bigger than I filed. This week the continuous WTI series rolled, so I compare December with December: $99.02 to $103.44 Friday evening, about +$4.42, provisional. Brent's December contract did more — $109.86 to $116.91, past $117 intraday per CBS, the highest of the war. The reason was a claim: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four tankers were hit and three struck mines near Hormuz on Thursday; Trump called it fabricated. Kpler had flows near 14 mb/d, better than last week. XLE closed $69.33 (+1.6%), another 52-week closing high, with Exxon, Chevron, Conoco and EOG at highs beside it. The refiners went the other way: Valero earned $23.90 a share and fell 5.7%.
